title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a 'formulaire' (reference sheet of formulas) for GL(2,Z) begun on p.29. Notation: g(x) means the conjugate g x g^{-1}. The matrices are: rho (order 6, rotating the three cusps 0, 1, inf); omega = -id; the sigma_i (order 4); the unipotents eps_i; rho_i = eps_i^2, which generate the level-2 congruence subgroup Gamma(2) and satisfy rho_inf rho_1 rho_0 = omega; the reflections tau_i; and tau'_i = sigma_i tau_i.

(1) Action of the reflections on the other generators. For i != j, tau_i inverts eps_j, rho_j and rho'_j. The exceptional cases are expressed through conjugations, e.g. tau_inf(rho_inf) = omega rho_0 rho_1 = rho_1^{-1}(rho_inf^{-1}) = rho_0(rho_inf^{-1}). Further: tau_i(sigma_i) = sigma_i^{-1}; tau'_i(rho) = rho^{-1}; tau_i(rho) = rho'^{-1}_{i-1} rho = sigma_i(rho^{-1}). The sigma_i swap the other two cusps, e.g. sigma_i(rho_{i+1}) = rho_{i+2}, and sigma_i(rho_i) = omega(rho_{i+1}rho_{i+2})^{-1}.

(2) Three-generator presentation of SL(2,Z). Set lambda_0 = eps_0 (parabolic), lambda_1 = sigma_inf (order 4), lambda_inf = rho^{-1} (order 6). Then lambda_inf lambda_1 lambda_0 = 1. This makes SL(2,Z) a quotient of pi_{0,3} = pi_1(P^1 minus {0,1,inf}), the free group <l_0, l_1, l_inf | l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1>, with the inertia orders (inf, 4, 6). Equivalently, it is the (2,3,inf) orbifold structure of the modular curve, lifted from PSL to SL.

(3) Extension by reflections. Set Gamma_0 = tau'_inf = [[0,1],[1,0]], Gamma_1 = -tau'_0 = [[-1,1],[0,1]], Gamma_inf = tau_inf = diag(-1,1). These satisfy:
- Gamma_inf Gamma_1 = lambda_0,
- Gamma_0 Gamma_inf = lambda_1,
- Gamma_1 Gamma_0 = lambda_inf.
Hence there is a commutative square: phi from pi_{0,3}^tau (the extension of pi_{0,3} by complex conjugation, generated by three reflections tau_i with l_i = products of consecutive reflections) onto GL(2,Z), restricting to phi^0 from pi_{0,3} onto SL(2,Z). Both maps are surjective.

(4) Presentations.
- SL(2,Z) = <rho, sigma | rho^3 = rho^{-3} = sigma^2>, i.e. Z/6 *_{Z/2} Z/4.
- GL(2,Z) = SL(2,Z) semidirect <tau'>, with tau' inverting rho and sigma.
- GL(2,Z) = <Gamma_0, Gamma_1, Gamma_inf | Gamma_i^2 = 1, (Gamma_0 Gamma_inf)^2 = (Gamma_1 Gamma_0)^{+-3}>, i.e. D_6 *_{D_2} D_4. Here D_6 has order 12, D_4 has order 8, and the amalgam is over the Klein group <Gamma_0, omega>.

(5) Notational dictionary against the 1981 formulary: sigma_i is replaced by sigma_i^{-1}; l_i becomes rho_i; lambda_i becomes rho'_i = omega rho_i; l'_i becomes lambda_i.

Purpose: this is a bookkeeping layer for the genus-0 / genus-1 base of the Teichmüller tower. It identifies the modular group, with its real structure, as a quotient of the 'real' fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points. It prepares p.31, which lifts everything to the central extension SL(2,Z)~ = B_3 (braid relation eps0 eps1 eps0 = eps1 eps0 eps1) and to GL(2,Z)~.
errors: In the NB block the page writes Gamma_inf = sigma Gamma_0 = Gamma_0 sigma^{-1}. But sigma_inf Gamma_0 = [[1,0],[0,-1]] = omega Gamma_inf. The correct identity, consistent with Gamma_0 Gamma_inf = lambda_1 = sigma, is Gamma_inf = Gamma_0 sigma = sigma^{-1} Gamma_0. This is a sign (omega) slip.

The other relations I checked by matrix multiplication are correct: Gamma_inf Gamma_1 = eps_0, Gamma_0 Gamma_inf = sigma_inf, Gamma_1 Gamma_0 = rho^{-1}, tau_inf(rho_inf) = omega rho_0 rho_1 = rho_1^{-1}(rho_inf^{-1}) = rho_0(rho_inf^{-1}), tau_i(rho) = sigma_i(rho^{-1}), Gamma_1 = rho^{-1} Gamma_0 = Gamma_0 rho, and Gamma_1 = -tau'_0.

Notational overload: rho_i denotes both the matrices eps_i^2 and, in phi(rho_i) = lambda_i, the standard loop generators of pi_{0,3}. These are different elements; in fact phi does not send loops to the matrices rho_i.

ideas.what: SL(2,Z) as a quotient of pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) with local monodromies a parabolic, an order-4 and an order-6 element whose product is 1
ideas.modern_name: modular orbifold M_{1,1} as a (2,3,inf) orbifold (lifted to SL_2); Belyi/dessins viewpoint on the modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke); in the dessins framework Grothendieck's Esquisse and its later expositions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of SL(2,Z) / the cartographic group and M_{1,1}

ideas.what: Extension to GL(2,Z) via three reflections Gamma_i, products of consecutive ones giving lambda_i; pi_{0,3}^tau (pi_{0,3} extended by complex conjugation) mapping onto GL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: extended modular group as a reflection (Coxeter-type) triangle group; orientation-reversing / 'real' extension of the orbifold fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (extended modular group PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,inf) reflection group)
ideas.where_published: The cartographic group with reflections is discussed in the Esquisse; this explicit GL(2,Z) form is likely unpublished

ideas.modern_name: amalgam decompositions of SL_2(Z) and GL_2(Z) (Bass-Serre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Serre 'Trees' (1977) for the SL case, the GL case well known

ideas.what: Formulary of conjugation actions of reflections and order-4 elements on the level-2 generators rho_i, eps_i
ideas.modern_name: explicit action of GL(2,Z)/Gamma(2) = S_3 x Z/2 (times +-1) on Gamma(2), i.e. symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,inf}

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically carries the complex-conjugation ('tau') extension pi_{0,3}^tau alongside pi_{0,3} when describing the base of the Teichmüller tower. This means working with the real structure / Gal(C/R) from the start. It is a minor documentary point about his approach to the Teichmüller tower, not a new result.
missed.quote: on a pi_{0,3}^tau --phi--> Gl(2,Z) ... pi_{0,3} --phi^0--> Sl(2,Z), phi, phi^0 surj.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Slightly relevant to the history of 'real' or extended versions of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group and of the mapping class groups including orientation reversals. Mathematically it is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely classical computations: presentations of SL(2,Z) and GL(2,Z) as amalgams, triangle-group generators, and conjugation tables. Useful as a window into Grothendieck's bookkeeping for the Teichmüller tower with complex conjugation, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.

In the tau_inf(rho_inf) column the last line is rho_0(rho_inf^{-1}) (conjugate by rho_0); the transcribed exponent '2' on rho_0 is doubtful.
The final displayed line of the tau_inf(rho_inf) chain: '= rho_1^{-1}(rho_inf^{-1})' is correct as transcribed.
